eight paths

one program, eight doors. every door is built the same way and filled with its own words, its own stories, and its own texts. nothing is blended.

year one · the mountain

five camps, about a lesson a day. a few minutes a day.

camp 1 · first steps — 21 days. a word you've probably already said, the story under it, and a breath. "oh, this is easy."
camp 2 · the stories — about eleven weeks. the great stories of your door, told as a serial. "wait, this is good."
camp 3 · the practices — about nine weeks. what people in this faith actually do, and how. "I can do this."
camp 4 · the text — the central text, start to finish. "I actually read it."
camp 5 · the depths — the mystics, the hard questions, the parts nobody teaches you. "there's more?"

years two to five · the ranges

the texts underneath, the saints and teachers, the schools, the sources. some people stay five years. three of the five years are written and checked today; four and five are being written. the first hundred days are the on-ramp; the mountain is year one; the ranges are the rest of your life if you want them.

the eight doors, one line each

Christianity — first word: amen. the text: the Gospel of Mark, start to finish.
Catholicism — first word: grace. the text: the Psalms and a Gospel; the Mass, the rosary and the saints along the way.
Judaism — first word: shalom. the text: the weekly Torah portion — the calendar already runs the syllabus.
Islam — first word: salaam. the text: the short surahs every Muslim child knows, sound first, meaning second.
Hinduism — first word: namaste. the text: the Bhagavad Gita, all eighteen chapters.
Buddhism — first word: metta. the text: the Dhammapada, all twenty-six chapters.
Sikhism — first word: seva. the text: Japji Sahib, verse by verse.
my own path — first word: breathe. the practice without the belief; wisdom stories always tagged with where they came from, never blended into a teaching. Rumi, the Tao Te Ching, and Marcus Aurelius as companions.

already know some?

a short check puts you where you belong — anywhere on the path, up to year three for now. if it placed you too far, the path offers to walk you back, and nothing you've done is lost. days are earned; position isn't — day one is always day one, whatever lesson you start on.

the door rule

a door opens when a religion has one word, one Keeper, one voice, and a first camp. more doors are coming. tell us which.

start now. it's free.
